items.title: Performance & Talent Programs Manager
items.location_text: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY; Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are seeking an experienced People Programs Manager to join our Performance & Talent Programs team. This role will own the design and end-to-end execution of some of Anthropic's performance and talent programs producing the year-round performance signal that feeds our talent intelligence layer and upholds our performance bar as we scale. This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Performance & Talent Programs, and a great fit for a true builder who has both seen performance management excellence at scale and is excited to roll up their sleeves in a rapidly scaling, high-ambiguity environment. You will also work closely with our internal products team, helping guide product decisions as we build and design the architecture that supports performance. Key responsibilities Own end-to-end execution of some of Anthropic's cyclical performance and talent programs (performance pulses, promotions, review cycles, talent reviews, succession planning, etc) and the continuous feedback practices between them Ensure these programs scale durably and uphold Anthropic's performance bar and talent density as the company grows Design programs to produce useful performance signal year-round and feed it into the talent intelligence layer to inform talent planning decisions Partner cross-functionally with People Services on cycle execution, People Analytics on connecting performance data to broader people data and insights, and People Products and engineering on program tooling Act as the product partner for our internal tools team: bring the needs of managers, employees, and People Partners to the table, help decide what to build and in what order, and shape the architecture so our performance systems connect cleanly and scale Iterate on program frameworks (calibration, rating constructs, feedback formats, promotion criteria) based on data, manager feedback, and Anthropic's evolving needs Lead program redesigns and change management, including stakeholder alignment, rollout planning, and communications Develop and deliver enablement that helps managers and People Partners run each cycle confidently and consistently Minimum qualifications Systems thinker who treats programs as performance drivers, caring as much about data quality and downstream usefulness as about cycles landing on time Demonstrated experience shaping performance tooling (Workday, Lattice, CultureAmp, or homegrown), including time working with an internal tools or engineering team to guide product decisions, and partnering with People Analytics, with comfort getting into the data yourself Experience building manager enablement that changes behavior, and supporting leaders through performance, promotion, and talent conversations Strong program management skills and operational rigor, with a track record of running complex multi-month cycles and keeping dozens of stakeholders in sync Exceptional communicator, particularly in writing, who thrives in ambiguity and evolving scope Preferred qualifications 7+ years of experience designing, running, and owning performance management, talent review, or promotion programs, preferably through periods of rapid headcount growth Experience helping define requirements, priorities, and system design for internal people tools, from early idea through adoption The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $240,000 — $240,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Program Manager, Local Community Impact
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our Community team builds direct relationships with people who use OpenAI’s technology, helps others learn from their experiences, and brings their insights back to product and research teams. Our programs connect communities with trusted partners who help organizations adopt AI effectively. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Program Manager to build and run our partner network. You will turn an early program into a reliable operation: recruit and onboard partners, coordinate agreements and payments, manage external service providers, support local events and marketing, review service quality, and improve the program as we learn. This partner network will be on the ground in communities helping people–from small businesses, non-profits, and community organizations–experience concrete benefits from our technology. They will set up useful workflows, learn OpenAI tools and become more confident, independent users. You should be as comfortable helping a partner resolve an onboarding issue as you are designing the systems that prevent it from happening again. You will work with local operators and internal teams to make sure commitments are clear, work gets done, and the people we serve receive useful, high-quality support. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Build the partner operating model, from sourcing and selection of partners through onboarding, ongoing support, renewal and exit. Establish clear expectations, owners, timelines and escalation paths. Create a scalable operating model that supports program growth and evolving partner needs. - Run partner onboarding with Legal, Finance and Procurement: track agreements, required information, vendor setup, readiness and start dates so partners can begin work and receive payments through approved processes. - Manage partner payments, reporting and related operational processes. - Plan and support local workshops, deployments and events with partners. Coordinate audiences, venues, budgets, materials, staffing and follow-up while preserving local ownership. - Coordinate program marketing and communications with Community, Marketing and content partners. Develop clear partner guidance, route brand and messaging approvals, and help useful stories and practices reach the right audiences. - Build trusted relationships with local operators and the organizations they serve. Coach partners, answer questions, address service-quality concerns and set clear boundaries around access, funding and program participation. - Create practical systems for the partner community: intake, a shared knowledge base, service logs, regular check-ins and reusable playbooks that reduce manual work without sacrificing quality. - Develop and operate partner review processes with the hiring manager and relevant teams. Combine verified service delivery, beneficiary feedback and sustained product use to understand performance and improve support. - Collaborate with analytics and product teams to assess program impact using appropriate data and feedback. - Manage budgets, vendors, risks and dependencies across the program. Keep stakeholders informed, surface decisions early and bring recurring partner feedback into program and product improvements. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - 8+ years owning a complex partner, community or operational program from early design through execution at scale, with clear examples of what you personally built and improved. - Bring strong operational judgment and follow-through across onboarding, financial workflows, events and multiple stakeholder groups. - Can earn trust with small-business owners, local technical operators and community leaders, explain expectations plainly and have difficult conversations when needed. - Have practical familiarity with ChatGPT, Codex and AI-enabled workflows, and can work credibly with technical specialists while explaining tools to people with less technical experience. - Use data and qualitative feedback to distinguish meaningful outcomes from activity counts, and can improve a process without making it unnecessarily bureaucratic. - Write clearly, communicate risks early, work independently through ambiguity and collaborate effectively across teams. - Have experience creating playbooks, support systems or automation that lets a high-touch program scale. NICE TO HAVE - Operating a local-services, small-business, nonprofit, fellowship, ambassador or distributed partner program. - Coordinating vendor onboarding, invoices, budgets or grant-like payment workflows with Finance and Legal. - Running hands-on workshops or community events and translating successful local practices into reusable resources. - Working across marketing, product, analytics and public-policy or regional teams. items.title: Knowledge & Operational Readiness Specialist
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Platforms Knowledge Management team's mission is to ensure Robinhood associates and customers have clear, current, and compliant guidance at their fingertips. We own the knowledge ecosystem — taxonomy, governance, editorial standards, and content lifecycle — and partner closely with CX Strategy, Product, Operations, Compliance, Legal, and Quality to publish SOPs and reusable messaging that are easy to find and use. As a Knowledge & Operational Readiness Specialist , you will own the content and readiness lifecycle for several assigned functions, partnering with senior team members on more complex work — driving knowledge strategy, leading readiness programs, and making meaningful program-level decisions with limited outside support. You lead cross-functional collaboration across all of your functions simultaneously, influence Product, Engineering, Compliance, and CX partners at all levels, and develop colleagues within the team. This is a role for someone who is equally fluent in SOPs and go/no-go frameworks, and uses AI to rethink what's possible. This role is based in our Denver, CO and Westlake, TX office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week (W,Th,F required) At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Own end-to-end content strategy and knowledge governance for assigned function(s): creation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Help Center articles, SOPs, runbooks, playbooks, escalation paths, policy documentation, and support workflows Lead readiness planning for product launches, policy updates, process changes, and operational initiatives — including go/no-go recommendations, risk registers, mitigation plans, and post-launch retrospectives Lead cross-functional collaboration across all assigned functions simultaneously — influencing Product, Engineering, Operations, Customer Support, Compliance, Risk, and Training partners at all levels to drive alignment on readiness and content strategy Establish content standards, information architecture, and governance frameworks that scale across functions and raise the bar for the team Partner with Customer Support leadership to prepare frontline teams for launches; identify contact drivers and support risks before go-live and develop plans to minimize customer friction Analyze metrics across assigned function(s) to identify patterns, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities; drive post-launch reviews and lead improvement initiatives Communicate readiness status, performance insights, and risks to stakeholders at all levels, from operational detail to executive-ready narratives Guide, coach, and share functional expertise with colleagues within the team; influence parties inside and outside the department on knowledge management processes and practices Use AI to tackle domain-specific knowledge problems — not just speed up routine work. The bar: streamlined workflows, resolved bottlenecks, and consistently higher-quality outcomes delivered faster. What you bring Experienced individual contributor with advanced knowledge of knowledge management and content strategy, and practical experience across multiple related job areas — typically 3-4+ years of relevant experience Proven track record of independently owning multiple functions end-to-end and making meaningful program-level decisions with limited outside support Deep knowledge management and content strategy background: governance, information architecture, content lifecycle, and knowledge base operations Leads cross-functional collaboration and influences Product, Engineering, Compliance, and CX partners across all levels across multiple assigned functions Executive-level communication: able to move between granular operational detail and leadership-ready narratives depending on the audience Strong project management skills; comfortable holding multiple workstreams simultaneously without losing quality Uses AI to tackle hard, domain-specific problems — not just to speed up work but to rethink what's possible Active FINRA licenses where functionally necessary; deep subject matter expertise in assigned function(s) What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance-driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Best-in-class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $94,000 — $110,000 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $82,000 — $97,000 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $73,000 — $86,000 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

This exciting career opportunity offers a blend of operational oversight and cross-functional collaboration. items.title: Staff / Senior Data Center Security Engineer
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer for one or more security domains end to end: design the controls, build the systems that enforce and verify them, and set the technical standard the rest of the team and our partners build to. The engineering is in the controls and the tooling that proves them. The goal is security that runs itself: requirements kept as code and checked automatically, evidence, chain of custody and access continuously verified, and tools and agents in place of manual reviews. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. This is a foundational role: you'll shape how our security engineering is built and scaled. The team's physical security systems engineers design and test the site security systems themselves; this role engineers the controls around them and across the domains beyond the facility itself: hardware custody, media, personnel and vendors. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, Anthropic's compute, data center operations, legal, compliance and procurement teams, and directly with data center operators, hardware vendors and logistics providers. The role involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure, and may include on-call for security events at them. Key responsibilities Security domains, end to end: own one or more of physical security at partner-operated and Anthropic-operated sites, hardware supply chain and chain of custody, media protection and sanitization, personnel security and site access, third-party and vendor security assessment, and maintenance and contingency controls Tools, automation and AI agents: build the internal tools, automation and agents the team runs on: evidence collection, access reviews, asset and custody tracking, partner intake. When a process keeps costing people time, you build the tool that retires it Security review for new sites, leases and vendors: find the gaps in the design, the contract and the operator's procedures, write the security terms and exhibits, and verify the fixes after signing Requirements and procedures as code: write requirements and procedures that a partner can build to and an assessor can test, kept as code in a version-controlled repository Site and supplier assessment: assess sites and suppliers against those requirements, on site and from evidence; document deviations and engineer the compensating control where a requirement can't be met as written Continuous compliance evidence: tie controls to the compliance frameworks we and our partners are assessed against, with evidence always current so an assessment pulls from it directly Security event response: respond to security events at sites (intrusion alarms, custody breaks, access violations) with operations teams and site operators; write up what happened and fix the control that allowed it Minimum qualifications Have engineered a security control domain end to end: designed the controls, built or integrated the systems that enforce them, and verified they work Read and review code, design the data systems behind security tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review Have done security work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet, in at least one of the domains under Key responsibilities Have applied a control framework such as NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001 or SOC 2 to real systems and produced the evidence for it Write requirements a third party can build to and an assessor can test: each states what must be true, how it is verified and what evidence shows it Preferred qualifications Experience across several of the domains above rather than one Experience at sites you did not fully control: cloud, colocation or GPU cloud operators Experience with federal assessment regimes based on NIST SP 800-53, including supply chain (NIST SP 800-161) and media sanitization (NIST SP 800-88) guidance; have produced evidence an assessor accepted Have built governance, risk and compliance (GRC) or evidence automation: automated control checks, asset or custody tracking, questionnaire and assessment pipelines, docs-as-code workflows Have run incident response at physical sites: alarms, investigations, after-action fixes Have worked in live data halls and on active construction sites, and can follow a method of procedure Experience redlining contract security language with legal and procurement counterparts Experience with international sites: per-country personnel screening and staffing restrictions, data residency, and export controls on hardware Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual security work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Senior Software Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic. The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch. You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next. We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way. The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time. What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on. This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you. or cluster computing environments Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role Overview Cohere has a strong AI narrative, the most deployable product, and a CEO who co-authored the foundational paper of modern AI. Following its recent partnership with Aleph Alpha, the company is positioned to become the transatlantic leader in sovereign AI for enterprise and government, and needs a storytelling engine to deliver that story at scale. This role sits within the team that is building that engine. In this cross functional role, you will stand up our PR and Communications function in the German market. You'll partner with the Global Corporate Communications team and EMEA Communications team to create a regional communication plan that fuels our growth among governments and enterprises in the most highly-regulated industries across DACH. You’ll nurture how we talk to customers, partners, and employees, ensuring that the corporate message resonates culturally for the German market and its audiences. This is a rare opportunity to build a comprehensive German PR function at a fast-growing company in the most dynamic space in technology. This is a role for someone who likes to take big swings – and have fun doing it – where no job is too big or too small. Key Responsibilities As the Communications Manager for Germany, you will: - Own and drive Cohere’s German communications strategy, aligning corporate priorities, business objectives, product innovation, executive visibility and technical differentiation to strengthen the company’s reputation in Germany - Translate Cohere’s innovations and customer success stories into compelling, locally relevant narratives for German-speaking audiences - Lead proactive media engagement and newsjacking opportunities in close collaboration with EMEA Communications and EMEA Government Affairs, capitalising on relevant industry and policy developments to amplify Cohere’s voice - Elevate the profile and influence of Cohere’s German leadership and spokespeople by partnering with Executive Communications to develop strategic messaging, thought leadership, media opportunities and executive visibility programmes, including for the German Country Manager. - Strengthen Cohere’s reputation through customer- and partner-led storytelling, working closely with Partner Marketing to showcase German customer outcomes, deepen strategic relationships and amplify the impact of Cohere’s ecosystem in the local market. - Lead and coordinate German crisis and issues communications, partnering with Corporate Communications and relevant local and regional teams to anticipate reputational risks, develop response strategies and ensure clear and timely communications. Qualifications - Have 7-10 years of experience in B2B communications in DACH, or technical content, ideally in AI, enterprise software, or developer‑focused environments - Have a talent for translating complex topics into different languages without losing nuance - Are experienced at managing PR agencies in the German market - Have experience and/or heavy interest in policy and regulatory communications, particularly within the German/EU regulatory environment - Have experience running communications strategies for the DACH region - Are highly organized and detail‑oriented with strong project management skills and a bias for action - Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and thrive in fast‑moving, high‑growth environments - Build strong cross‑functional relationships to drive clarity, consistency, and alignment across teams FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.title: Art Director
items.description: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the Opportunity We’re looking for a hands-on Art Director to help develop and make work across campaigns, research launches, and social. In the near term, you’ll focus on supporting research-related creative projects and launches, with opportunities to contribute more broadly. You’re a visual thinker and a maker: someone who can find a strong visual idea, build a quick prototype, and carry it through to execution. You bring craft, curiosity, and resourcefulness, and enjoy creating content across mediums with a small team, a short timeline, or an evolving brief. You’ll bring art direction and visual storytelling to projects that turn complex technology into ideas people connect with. Working closely with creative leads, copywriters, designers, and other creative partners, you’ll develop the visual approach and bring a distinctive point of view from concept through execution. This role is based in New York City and works across campaign and social, in close collaboration with OpenAI’s Creative, Marketing, Product, and Communications teams. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence. We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction. About the role We’re looking for a senior operations leader to own the Trusted Access operating strategy and lead a team of risk-operations specialists. You will set priorities across programs, build a reliable customer access service, and hire, manage, and develop your direct reports. This role combines program ownership with formal people management. You will establish shared commitments with technical support and regional escalation leaders, who manage their own teams, and bring those groups together around customer outcomes. You’ll stay close enough to complex cases to challenge assumptions while giving specialists the ownership and capacity to fix recurring problems. Success means customers reach the right access outcome with clear communication, teams make consistent decisions, and the service scales with less avoidable escalation and manual work. In this role, you will: - Own the operating strategy and roadmap across Trusted Access programs, translating customer needs and organizational priorities into clear service commitments, ownership, and investment decisions. - Build a coherent customer journey from application and eligibility review through approval, provisioning coordination, and confirmed access, including appeals and subsequent access changes. Establish clear handoffs and route exceptions to authorized decision-makers. - Hire, coach, and develop your team. Set expectations, delegate meaningful ownership, give direct feedback, address performance gaps, and build the capabilities needed as programs grow. - Make capacity and prioritization decisions across urgent customer needs, launch readiness, and lasting improvements. Coordinate regional coverage, vendor support, and backup with partner teams while protecting time to eliminate recurring work. - Lead consequential customer escalations, bringing incomplete or conflicting evidence into a clear decision process. Align owners on the next action and ensure customers receive accurate updates and a clear resolution. - Turn support patterns into a prioritized roadmap with Product and Engineering: improve onboarding, provisioning workflows, tooling, self-service, and AI-assisted operations. Validate that changes work before expanding them. - Establish measures of service health and decision quality. Align support responsibilities, review standards, customer guidance, and technical dependencies; make readiness gaps and tradeoffs clear to leadership. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have built and run complex customer support, onboarding, access, risk, or service operations, with measurable improvements beyond handling more volume. - Have formally managed people through hiring, development, difficult feedback, and performance decisions, and can show how your leadership increased the team’s capability and ownership. 5+ years of management experience preferred. - Can make defensible tradeoffs among customer commitments, safeguards, service quality, and capacity, even when stakeholders disagree or the evidence is incomplete. - Have led work across teams you do not manage, resolving ownership gaps and negotiating commitments that hold up in execution. - Are analytically and technically fluent enough to diagnose workflow failures, evaluate automation, and partner effectively on product and provisioning changes. - Communicate with precision and empathy, from explaining an access blocker to a customer to presenting a difficult investment decision to leadership. items.title: Incubation Management Lead
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket ships fast. New products, new market types, new payment rails, new geographies: the pace is real and it does not slow down for anyone. The Customer Experience team's job is to make sure that speed does not come at the cost of the people using the platform. Right now, CX readiness for new launches is a gap we need to close, and this role closes it. You will own launch readiness for CX end to end. That means getting into product planning early, building the readiness plan, standing up a small pilot support pod, and running it until the launch is stable enough to hand off to our scaled operation or external partners. You will write the playbook as you go, because in many cases nobody has supported this type of product before. The team you will work with spans support operations, enablement, and external partners, and you will be the connective tissue between all of them and the Product teams shipping new things. This is a builder role. If you need a defined process to work within, this is not the right fit. If you are energized by figuring out how to support something that has never been supported before, and then making sure the next person does not have to figure it out from scratch, this is exactly the right fit. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build and own the CX readiness plan for every new product, market type, and geography launch, from kickoff through stable handoff. - Embed with Product teams at the planning stage to surface support needs, flag risks, and make sure CX requirements are scoped in before engineering is done. - Stand up and directly manage pilot support pods for new launches, including staffing, tooling, and day-to-day operations during the incubation period. - Work with the Enablement team to produce training materials, SOPs, and QA criteria before each launch goes live. - Track contact rates, issue trends, and customer satisfaction data for newly launched products and report findings back to Product with clear recommendations. - Define the criteria for what "stable" looks like for each launch, and execute the handoff to scaled operations or external partners once those criteria are met. - Build the readiness framework for international expansion, accounting for language, regulatory context, and partner capability as Polymarket enters new markets. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 4 or more years in support operations, program management, or product operations, with direct ownership of launch readiness or go-live planning. - Demonstrated experience launching new products, market types, or geographies from the support side, including building SOPs and training from scratch. - Track record of strong cross-functional partnership with Product and Engineering teams, not just coordination but actual influence on how products are built and scoped. - Comfort operating in ambiguity: you have built processes where none existed and made good decisions without complete information. - Strong written communication, you can write a clear readiness plan, a crisp status update, and a useful post-launch report without someone editing it for you. - Organized and reliable follow-through: teams and partners depend on you to track details and close loops without being chased. - (Plus) Experience at a startup or high-growth company where the roadmap changed fast and you had to adapt your plans to match. - (Plus) Experience managing international or multi-geography launches, including working with external support partners across different time zones and languages. BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $200,000 to $250,000, plus equity and benefits. This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

items.title: Senior Software Engineer, Observability
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Observability team's mission is to build and own Robinhood's full-stack observability platform — the foundation that keeps every product, service, and customer experience running reliably at scale. We design and operate the systems that give engineers deep visibility into how Robinhood's infrastructure behaves, ensuring that when something goes wrong, the right people know immediately and can act fast. Our work spans metrics, logs, distributed tracing, and alerting pipelines, and we partner closely with the Robinhood Command Center to ensure our observability systems meet or exceed 99.9% uptime. We believe in monitoring our own monitors — the observability infrastructure is a product, not just a tool. As a Senior Software Engineer on the Observability team, you will be the technical lead shaping the roadmap for how Robinhood observes itself at scale. You will own the observability control plane end-to-end, making architectural decisions that directly impact the reliability and operational health of Robinhood's entire product surface. You'll lead a team of six engineers, drive the strategy for cost-efficient telemetry ingestion, build in-house solutions where off-the-shelf tooling falls short, and integrate AI-driven approaches to accelerate progress toward full-stack observability. This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role where your technical decisions set the direction for the entire organization! This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you'll do Define and execute the full-stack observability roadmap, establishing a clear technical vision for metrics, logs, traces, and alerting infrastructure across Robinhood's engineering organization. Own and evolve the observability control plane, including telemetry ingestion pipelines, cost management strategies, and the tooling that ensures observability components remain highly available. items.title: Customer Success Manager, Public Sector & Defence
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! WHY THIS ROLE? We're seeking an exceptional Customer Success Manager with deep expertise in the Canadian public sector and defence landscape to lead our most strategic government accounts. This role requires an individual who understands both the transformative potential of frontier AI and the unique requirements of government and defence organizations. You will be the trusted advisor and strategic partner for Canadian federal departments, provincial agencies, Crown corporations, defence organizations, and healthcare systems as they navigate the complex journey of AI adoption. You'll guide organizations through the implementation of frontier AI in secure, highly regulated environments—ensuring solutions deliver a measurable impact while meeting stringent security, privacy, compliance, and ethical requirements. In this role, you'll collaborate with our Strategic Customer team, Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform, Product, and Go-to-Market teams, serving as the voice of the customer internally and the face of Cohere externally for our most sensitive and high-impact government engagements. You'll have the unique opportunity to shape how Canada's most important institutions leverage AI to serve the public good. Location: Ottawa (proximity to government customers) Security Clearance: Active Top Secret clearance is mandatory for this role WHAT YOU'LL DO Strategic Customer Partnership: - Own the success, adoption, and growth of Cohere's Canadian public sector and defence customers, ensuring they realize maximum value from our AI solutions - Build deep, trusted relationships with senior government stakeholders, including Deputy Ministers, CIOs, ADMs, digital transformation leads, and departmental executives - Develop comprehensive success plans tailored to each organization's mission, digital strategy, budget cycles, and unique constraints - Serve as the primary point of contact and executive sponsor for your accounts, managing escalations and ensuring customer satisfaction - Define and track success metrics aligned with public sector priorities: citizen satisfaction, service delivery improvements, cost savings, operational efficiency, accessibility outcomes AI Adoption & Implementation Leadership: - Guide customers through the full lifecycle of AI adoption—from use case identification and pilot design through production deployment and scaling - Lead secure AI implementation projects in complex government environments, including air-gapped systems, Protected B/C environments, and on-premises deployments - Navigate the unique challenges of public sector AI adoption: legacy system integration, data sensitivity, lengthy approval processes, and risk-averse organizational cultures - Create and execute change management strategies to drive user adoption and value realization across diverse government workforces - Conduct regular executive business reviews with senior stakeholders, demonstrating ROI, impact, and strategic value - Drive contract renewals and account growth by consistently delivering value and building trusted relationships Compliance & Risk Management: - Ensure all implementations meet Canadian government security protocols, including PBMM standards, security assessments, and authority-to-operate requirements - Navigate privacy and compliance requirements: Privacy Act, PIPEDA, PHIPA, Access to Information Act, Official Languages Act, accessibility standards - Lead or support Algorithmic Impact Assessments and responsible AI governance processes as required by Treasury Board directives - Develop risk mitigation strategies for AI deployments in high-security, mission-critical, and citizen-facing contexts - Coordinate with customer security teams, privacy officers, legal counsel, and compliance functions Customer Advocacy & Product Influence: - Serve as the voice of public sector and defence customers within Cohere, advocating for features and capabilities that address government-specific needs - Provide strategic feedback to Product and Engineering teams on requirements related to security, explainability, accessibility, bilingualism, and ethical AI - Contribute to the development of public sector-specific offerings, implementation playbooks, documentation, and best practices - Share customer insights to inform Cohere's public sector go-to-market strategy and positioning - Represent Cohere at government forums, working groups, roundtables, and industry events Cross-Functional Collaboration: - Partner with Sales to support expansion opportunities, renewals, and new customer acquisition - Coordinate with Solutions Architects and Forward Deployed Engineers on technical implementation and optimization - Work with Legal, Security, and Compliance teams to navigate complex procurement, contracting, and regulatory requirements - Collaborate with Marketing on thought leadership content, case studies, and public sector community building YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF: Required Experience: - 8+ years of experience in customer success, account management, strategic consulting, or technology delivery roles within enterprise or government contexts - At least 3-5 years working directly with the Canadian government, defence, or healthcare organizations in a technology, digital transformation, or consulting capacity - Proven track record of managing complex, strategic accounts with multiple stakeholders, long sales cycles, and multi-year implementation timelines - Experience leading AI/ML, cloud, or enterprise software implementations in secure or highly regulated environments - Deep understanding of how government organizations evaluate, procure, implement, and govern technology solutions - Active Top Secret security clearance (mandatory) Customer Success & Account Management Excellence: - Demonstrated success driving customer adoption, expansion, and retention in complex enterprise or government accounts - Experience developing and executing customer success strategies, QBRs, and executive engagement programs - Track record of identifying and closing expansion opportunities within existing accounts - Ability to manage multiple strategic accounts simultaneously while maintaining high-touch, personalized engagement - Experience navigating organizational politics and building coalitions across siloed government departments Public Sector & Defence Acumen: - Comprehensive knowledge of the Canadian public sector ecosystem: federal departments, provincial ministries, Crown corporations, defence, intelligence, critical infrastructure, and healthcare - Deep familiarity with government digital strategies, service delivery transformation, and citizen-centric design principles - Understanding of public sector budget cycles, Treasury Board processes, government procurement frameworks, and contract vehicles - Knowledge of relevant legislation and frameworks: Privacy Act, PIPEDA, PHIPA, Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessments, accessibility requirements - Experience with government cloud strategies and security frameworks: GC Cloud, PBMM, Protected environments, CCCS guidelines - Proven ability to work with classified information and operate effectively in secure, compartmented environments Nice to Have: - Bilingual (English/French) proficiency—a strong asset for working across the federal government - 3+ years specifically managing GenAI, LLM, or conversational AI implementations - Experience with specific Canadian public sector digital transformation initiatives: Canada.ca http://Canada.ca modernization, healthcare AI projects, Canadian Digital Service programs, or provincial digital government initiatives - Direct experience working with Canadian defence, intelligence, public safety, or national security organizations - Professional certifications: CSM, PMP, ITIL, or Canadian government-specific security training - Experience with government collaboration platforms: GCdocs, GCworkspace, Protected collaboration tools - Background in management consulting, systems integration, or digital transformation consulting for public sector clients - Experience with any modern programming language (C++, C#, JavaScript, Python, etc.) WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE UNIQUE This is a rare opportunity to shape how Canada's most important institutions leverage AI to serve the public good. You'll work with organizations responsible for national security, healthcare delivery, social services, and democratic institutions—helping them navigate the profound opportunities and responsibilities that come with deploying frontier AI technology. You'll need to balance competing demands: innovation velocity with government due diligence, technical possibilities with policy constraints, commercial success with public sector values, and breakthrough capabilities with ethical considerations. It requires patience, strategic thinking, in-depth sector knowledge, security awareness, and a genuine passion for achieving public service outcomes. If you're energized by complex challenges, have deep public sector expertise, understand the gravity of working with classified systems, and want to have an outsized impact on Canada's digital future while working with cutting-edge AI technology, this role is for you. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. THE ROLE You'll lead marketing operations and analytics at Cohere. That covers the team, the martech stack, how we measure marketing's contribution to pipeline, and the budget and pipeline numbers marketing plans against. When leadership asks what marketing produced last quarter and what to fund next, the answer starts with your numbers. The role reports to the VP of Brand. You'll work most closely with the Marketing Chief of Staff and the heads of Growth and Demand and Product Marketing, and every week with Revenue Operations, Sales Operations & Finance. Web operations is part of marketing but doesn't report to this role. WHAT YOU'LL OWN THE TEAM You'll manage the marketing operations, automation, and analytics and data operations staff, and hire where you find gaps. Marketing is growing rapidly, so you'll also bring acquired companies' systems and data into our stack. MEASUREMENT The attribution methodology is yours, documented and signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. Each quarter you'll present marketing's pipeline contribution to the executive team and say what you'd change. Your analysts do the same for the program teams in Growth and Demand, Events and Product Marketing, showing which campaigns and channels are paying back their spend. SYSTEMS AND DATA Marketo, Looker, GA4 and 6sense are yours end to end, along with the campaign and lead side of Salesforce. That includes forms, nurture, lead lifecycle, scoring and routing. Campaign data needs to be structured well enough that analysts don't need workarounds, and target-account data has to reconcile to the governed account list. With Revenue Operations, you'll make sure the data behind marketing's pipeline numbers can't change without a record, so a bulk edit can't quietly rewrite marketing's results. A/B testing on nurture and forms sits with you too, sized so the results can be read. Over time we want fewer tools and fewer dashboards, with one governed source for each metric. BUDGET AND PLANNING NUMBERS You'll own the martech and operations budget and track budget and headcount across marketing. You'll also build the pipeline and capacity models marketing plans against. The Marketing Chief of Staff runs planning and the business reviews and leads the trade-off conversations with your numbers in hand. Marketing and Sales need to count pipeline the same way, every time. YOUR FIRST YEAR In the first 90 days, you'll document the attribution methodology and get it signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. By then we should also have an inventory of every reporting surface, each with a named owner, and your order for fixing the data problems you inherit. By three months, one governed executive dashboard has replaced the competing decks in business reviews, and rebuilt lead routing is in production. By six months, target-account reporting reconciles to the governed list, and anyone on the team can reproduce quarterly attribution from the documented method, with change control on the data underneath it. You'll be embedded in the O2C Transformation team, working closely with Order Management, AR & Collections, Revenue Accounting, Billing Engineering, and Go-to-Market. You'll design and run the pricing audits and accuracy measures that show us where we leak revenue or create rework, then fix the root cause at the source. You'll be the compliance advocate for global O2C, helping the business find the compliant way to yes, and often improving a process by removing steps rather than adding them. You'll thrive here if you treat accuracy and compliance as design problems and as a service to the business. You are firm when the risk is real, flexible when it isn't, and able to explain the difference. If you're energized by ambiguous, high-consequence operational problems at a company at the forefront of AI development, we'd like to hear from you. Key responsibilities Design and run recurring audit programs across the O2C lifecycle, including pricing audits, contract-to-invoice accuracy, credits, refunds and concessions, and cash application Define accuracy metrics with baselines and targets, such as pricing and invoice error rates, first-pass yield, rework volume, and revenue leakage, and report them in a way teams can act on Trace findings to root cause and work with the owning team on the fix, whether in process, system configuration, or contract and pricing standards Move measurement from periodic sampling to continuous, system-driven monitoring as volume grows Partner with Order Management and AR operations as their quality partner, and help GTM, Deal Desk, Sales Operations, and Product understand what accurate and compliant looks like through clear published guidance that shortens the path to yes Review new processes, process changes, commercial models, and exceptions against policy and control requirements, with clear decision rights, service levels, and rationale that stay consistent across regions, entities, and channels Build compliance into new products, channels, commercial models, and regions by joining at intake rather than at the end Own O2C policies, control ownership, and segregation of duties Partner with Internal Audit, external auditors, Revenue Accounting, Tax, and Legal so audit cycles run smoothly, and resolve findings at the root cause Perform independent review activities, including month-end close reviews, so operations teams can focus on execution while independence is preserved Create reusable, pre-approved process patterns and guardrails so teams can move quickly without a bespoke review every time, harmonizing globally and localizing only where statute requires Work with Billing Engineering, GTM Systems, and Business Technology to build controls and accuracy checks into the systems themselves, so quality scales with volume Deploy AI and automation for exception detection, reconciliation, anomaly detection, and evidence collection Minimum qualifications Hands-on experience designing and running audit, quality, or revenue assurance programs within order-to-cash, billing operations, or quote-to-cash Working knowledge of revenue recognition (ASC 606) and experience partnering with internal and external auditors Experience with contracting systems, billing platforms, or ERP systems (for example Salesforce, Stripe, or Workday Financials) Proficiency with SQL or similar tools for analyzing and testing transactional data Experience using automation or AI for monitoring, testing, or reporting Preferred qualifications 10+ years of progressive experience in revenue operations, billing operations, revenue assurance, finance operations, or internal controls within order-to-cash at a public company A track record of simplifying processes, with concrete examples of steps or controls you removed while improving accuracy or strengthening the control environment A degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Engineering, or a related field CPA, CIA, CISA, or CRISC certification, or Lean Six Sigma or PMP certification Experience building or scaling a SOX program, including readiness for public-company reporting requirements Experience with global, multi-entity operations, including statutory invoicing and tax considerations Experience serving both B2C and B2B customers, especially with consumption-based and subscription billing models through to collections Experience working with go-to-market, deal desk, and revenue operations items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a senior B2B Growth Marketer to build and scale demand generation for ElevenLabs in India. This is a hands-on, in-country role focused on generating enterprise pipeline, growing our brand with technical buyers, and creating programs that become benchmarks for B2B marketing in AI. Your work will shape how Indian businesses discover, evaluate, and adopt ElevenLabs. The goal is to build repeatable marketing engines that make ElevenLabs the top choice for every enterprise. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build integrated B2B marketing campaigns end to end across India's priority industries from strategy and messaging through execution and measurement. - Localize and execute programs across ABM, content, events, webinars, partner/customer marketing, executive branding, product launches, and outbound - choosing the right channel for the problem rather than owning a single function. - Adapt global campaigns and messaging for the Indian market, and feed local insights (buyer behavior, competitive dynamics, regulatory context) back to the global team. - Partner closely with local sales and the global product marketing, growth, and design teams to keep messaging consistent and execute high-impact campaigns. - Own pipeline generation and campaign performance for the market, using data to measure results, run experiments, and continuously improve what works. REQUIREMENTS - 5 to 7 years of experience at a high-growth technology company - you've built and scaled B2B demand generation programs that created measurable enterprise pipeline, and you know what moved the needle. - Ownership Pedigree: You have implemented growth and marketing projects from start to finish and held yourself accountable for the ROI. - Deep knowledge of the Indian market: its enterprise buyers, media landscape, and business culture, ideally with an existing network. - Work well without much process. This role spans multiple marketing functions and needs someone who sets priorities, spots opportunities, and moves quickly as our first marketer in the market. - Relentless commitment to excellence — a high bar for quality, clarity, and impact. - Curious about AI, follows the technology ecosystem closely, and has exceptional judgment on what makes marketing stand out. #LI-Remote We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.
